seg_p0041_s0001: this, however, I report on the testimony of others, for I myself have not yet had the opportunity to see the author. The old translator of Chrysostom's sermon on Pentecost likewise intimates that he ran from Spain "into the farthest parts" of the earth. Finally, "like some heavenly bird ranging round about the inhabited world, having completed thirty-five years of gospel warfare for Christ," as Nicephorus writes, he at last consummated the course of his martyrdom at Rome under Nero.
seg_p0041_s0002: Aristobulus too, whom he (Paul) mentions in the Epistle to the Romans, I find recorded in the Greek Menaea as a bishop of the Britons ordained by Paul: where, on the fifteenth day of March, a commemoration of Aristobulus of this kind is made: Οὗτος ἦν εἷς τῶν ἑβδομήκοντα μαθητῶν, ἠκολούθησε δὲ τῷ ἁγίῳ ἀποστόλῳ Παύλῳ, κηρύττων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν οἰκουμένην διακονῶν αὐτῷ· ὑφ᾽ οὗ καὶ χειροτονεῖται ἐπίσκοπος εἰς τὴν τῶν Βρετανῶν χώραν, ἀγρίων ἀνδρῶν καὶ ὠμοτάτων· παρ᾽ ὧν ποτὲ μὲν τυπτόμενος, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ κατὰ τῆς ἀγορᾶς συρόμενος, πολλοὺς ἔπεισε τῷ Χριστῷ προσελθεῖν· ὅθεν καὶ ἐκκλησίας συστησάμενος, καὶ πρεσβυτέρους καὶ διακόνους ἐν αὐτῇ καταστήσας, ἐτελειώθη [This man was one of the seventy disciples, and he followed the holy apostle Paul, preaching the gospel throughout the whole inhabited world and ministering to him; by whom he was also ordained bishop for the land of the Britons, men savage and most brutal; at whose hands, being now beaten, now dragged through the marketplace, he persuaded many to come over to Christ; whence, having established churches and appointed presbyters and deacons in them, he reached the end of his life].
seg_p0041_fn_001: Volume 3 of the Latin edition, Paris 1546, and Basel 1558.
seg_p0041_fn_002: Οἷά τις πτηνὸς αἰθέριος ὁ Παῦλος διέθει, κύκλῳ διατρέχων τὴν οἰκουμένην [Paul sped on like some winged creature of the air, coursing round about the inhabited world]. Nicephorus Callistus, Ecclesiastical History, book 3, chapter 1. καθάπερ ὑποπτερός τις πᾶσαν διαδραμὼν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐσαγήνευσε [as some winged being, having run through the whole inhabited world, he drew it in as with a net]. Greek Menaea, June 29.
seg_p0041_fn_003: Πᾶσαν σχεδὸν τὴν γῆν διελθὼν, καὶ ἐπὶ πέντε καὶ τριάκοντα ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ διαθλεύσας ἐνιαυτοῖς [Having traversed almost the whole earth, and having contended for the gospel on behalf of Christ for thirty-five years]. Nicephorus, Ecclesiastical History, book 12, chapter 34. In barely the space of thirty years he brought the Romans, the Persians, the Parthians, the Medes, the Indians, the Scythians, the Sauromatae, the Saracens, and indeed the whole human race under the yoke of truth, etc. Chrysostom, Homily 4, On the Praises of Paul. Clement, in the Epistle to the Corinthians, page 8, concerning the same: Κῆρυξ γενόμενος ἐν τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὑτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν δικαιοσύνην διδάξαι ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν, καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου [Having become a herald in the east and in the west, he won the noble renown of his faith; teaching righteousness to the whole world, and having come to the limit of the west and borne witness as a martyr before the rulers, he thus departed from the world].
